title: Julia Quiz
description: Review the 12 starter lessons. The questions name the example to revisit. Take your time, use the lessons, and read the reason after each answer.

questions.question: println prints a value followed by a newline. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: println writes the String and ends the line. Use double quotes for strings.

questions.question: A variable gives a name to a value. The plus sign adds numbers. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: pencils holds 3. Adding 2 produces the separate result 5. Quoted numbers are text, not values for ordinary arithmetic.

questions.question: A dollar sign inserts a variable into a string. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The $name part is replaced with Ravi. Use $(...) when inserting a calculation.

questions.question: Julia arrays normally start at position 1. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: Julia counts from 1 here, so pets[2] is dog. A position outside the array raises an error.

questions.question: A dot applies an operation element by element. Here each number is doubled. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The dotted multiplication applies to each item. The results are 4 and 6. The dot is important when you want item-by-item operations.

questions.code:
score = 8
if score >= 5
 println("Pass")
else
 println("Try again")
end
questions.question: if selects steps using a true-or-false rule. end closes the block. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The condition is true, selecting the first println. Julia requires a Boolean condition, not a bare number.

questions.question: 1:3 is a range including both ends. A for loop visits each value. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The range includes 3. Each number is printed during one loop pass. Close the loop with end.

questions.question: A short function definition can use an equals sign. The expression is returned. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The short function returns n * 2. Input 4 yields 8. Calling a function needs parentheses around its inputs.

questions.question: Dict connects keys with values. The => pair operator joins a key and value. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The string title is a dictionary key whose value is Moon Trip. Missing bracket keys throw an error; get can supply a fallback.

questions.question: A tuple is a fixed group of values. You can unpack its positions into names. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: Tuple unpacking binds the second position to score, so it is 8. A tuple itself cannot be changed item by item.

questions.code: println([n * 2 for n in 1:4 if n > 2])
questions.question: A comprehension makes values from inputs and an optional filter. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The filter keeps 3 and 4, then the result expression doubles them. Read the filter before working out which values are included.

questions.code:
struct Book
 title::String
 pages::Int
end
book = Book("Moon Trip", 24)
println(book.pages)
questions.question: A struct defines a type with named fields. Ordinary structs are immutable. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The Book constructor stores 24 in pages. Dot access reads it. Use mutable struct only when fields really need changing.
